findings.title: apply_schedule accepts a nonexistent entry_id and returns success when the call carries no field to apply
findings.claim: Of the 8 heat_pump_optimizer actions whose schema accepts entry_id, 7 raise ServiceValidationError for an id no config entry has; apply_schedule, called with that bogus id and no other field (a payload its all-Optional schema accepts), returns {'updated': {}, 'reason': 'nothing to apply'} because its early return precedes _loaded_entries.
findings.mechanism: handle_apply_schedule returns 'nothing to apply' at services.py:979-980 before it resolves target_entry through _loaded_entries, so the entry guard every sibling action runs first is skipped on the empty call.

evidence.machine: macOS arm64 dev box (leads seat), export of 17f1c55fad1b
evidence.contention_note: count, contention-immune (D3 quiet window held by another lease)

findings.instrumented_symbol: custom_components.heatpump_optimizer.services:handle_apply_schedule (as registered by async_register_services, schema applied, awaited on FakeHass)

findings.proposed_fix_scope: resolve _loaded_entries(hass, target_entry) at the top of handle_apply_schedule, before the 'nothing to apply' return; extend the D10 action-exceptions check to call each action with the empty-but-valid payload

findings.title: frictionKey keys a moved policy file's real path apart from its canonical spelling: 34 of 34 split
findings.claim: For every one of the 34 policy-corpus files that counts.mjs:canon() spells at an old path (the 8 role contracts, 15 dimension briefs, 10 rules, dev/audit/README.md), policy_lint.mjs:frictionKey returns the real path for an id naming the real path and the canonical path for the canonical spelling or bare basename, so friction recorded against one contract lands under two histogram keys.
findings.mechanism: trackedFiles and the budgets canonicalise every path through canon(), but frictionKey looks the raw id up in POLICY_KEY_INDEX without canon(), so the real in-tree path is never folded onto the canonical key.
